items.label: f05-event-unsubscribe-leak
items.front: Two event mistakes from the delegates lesson, and the pattern that avoids the second?
items.back: Not unsubscribing (the publisher keeps the subscriber alive: a memory leak) and raising without a null check; raise with Clicked?.Invoke(this, EventArgs.Empty).

items.label: f03-async-void
items.front: Why is `async void` on a normal method a bug (outside event handlers)?
items.back: The caller gets no Task, so it cannot await it or observe failures; an exception escapes onto the synchronization context and can crash the process. Return Task instead.

items.label: f04-first-vs-firstordefault
items.front: LINQ bug hunt: First() vs FirstOrDefault() when nothing matches?
items.back: First() throws InvalidOperationException; FirstOrDefault() returns default (null for reference types), which the caller must then handle.

items.label: f01-null-length-crash
items.front: `string maybe = null; Console.WriteLine(maybe.Length);` What happens, and what are two safe alternatives?
items.back: NullReferenceException at runtime. Guard it: maybe?.Length ?? 0, or string.IsNullOrEmpty(maybe) before reading Length.

items.label: f02-throw-in-finally
items.front: Three exception-handling bugs from the bug hunt: an empty catch (Exception), missing using on disposables, and throwing inside finally. Why is the last one so nasty?
items.back: An exception thrown in finally replaces the one already propagating, so the real root cause is lost from logs and callers.

items.prompt: Why do the lesson and its bug hunt warn against calling `.Result` or `.Wait()` on a task?

choices.text: They turn the caller into async void, so any exception thrown by the awaited task is lost
They block the thread, and if the continuation needs that thread, both wait forever
They cancel the task after a default 30-second timeout, returning partial results
They return the task's value before it finishes, so you may read a default value

choices: They turn the caller into async void, so any exception thrown by the awaited task is lost
They block the thread, and if the continuation needs that thread, both wait forever
They cancel the task after a default 30-second timeout, returning partial results
They return the task's value before it finishes, so you may read a default value

items.explanation: Sync-over-async blocks a thread the awaited continuation may need; awaiting all the way up avoids the deadlock.

decimal arithmetic is faster than double arithmetic, which matters on busy checkout pages

task2 cannot start until task1 has been awaited, so the whole block takes about 2 seconds
